title: Set a featherboard in the mitre slot to hold a board against the rip fence
instruction: Set the featherboard so it holds this board against the fence for the rip. Finish with both arms back where they started.
context: Before a rip on a table saw, a featherboard is set so its fingers keep the board against the fence as it is fed, stopping it wandering and helping prevent kickback. Saw manuals and woodworking guides give the setup: the board against the fence, the featherboard in the mitre slot ahead of the blade (Grizzly G0690 and G0661 manuals; Woodsmith), pressed in until its shorter setup feather just touches the board, and the knobs secured while it is held toward the stock and fence (Bench Dog Feather-Loc; Peachtree/Fulton). The job is a spring preload set by feel (fingers flexed 2 to 4 mm, 7 to 14 N) and kept through the locking, at a position measured from the blade. Carpenters (O*NET 47-2031.00, 889,700 US workers) list table saws among their tools and "Shape or cut materials ... using ... power saws"; cabinetmakers (O*NET 51-7011.00) "Set up or operate machines, including power saws".
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A 10 in contractor table saw (Delta 36-725T2 or any saw with a 27 in deep top, standard mitre slots and a T-square rip fence) set up for a rip, fixed: its top, 68.6 cm (27 in) front to back and 84 cm wide, 3.2 cm thick at the edge, spans 10 to 78.6 cm forward and 50 cm right to 34 cm left of the centre line, 85 cm above the floor (9 cm above the bench the arms stand on; the saw's stand is drawn as a short grey cabinet under it). The 10 in blade is wound fully down under the aluminium throat plate (35 x 9.2 cm); the plate's blade slot (1 cm wide) runs from 42 to 59 cm forward, 10 cm right of the centre line. The paddle switch on the front rail is off and the saw's cord is unplugged, lying on the bench. (2) The left mitre slot, 3/4 in wide and 3/8 in deep (19.05 x 9.5 mm), runs the length of the top 2.5 cm left of the centre line, 12.5 cm left of the blade. (3) The rip fence, locked on its front rail: a black steel fence 6 cm wide and 6.4 cm tall with laminate faces, the length of the top; its face is 20 cm right of the centre line, 10 cm right of the blade. (4) A 1x6 pine board (19 x 140 x 457 mm, 0.55 kg) lying flat, its long side along the fence and 15 mm off it (its left edge 4.5 cm right of the centre line), its front end 39.5 cm forward (1 in short of the blade slot), its back end overhanging the saw's front edge by 16 cm. (5) A mitre-slot featherboard modelled on the Bench Dog Single Feather-Loc (0.32 kg): an orange polymer body 27 x 14.5 cm and 1.7 cm deep with a row of 14 fingers (5.5 cm deep, 4.5 mm wide, 8.5 mm apart, leaning 30 degrees toward the blade) along its right-hand side and, at the near end of the row, a setup feather 3 mm shorter than the others (fingers and setup feather flexible polymer); under it, the maker's 7-1/2 in aluminium expanding mitre bar (68 g) in the left mitre slot; on top, two black T-knobs (58 mm wings) 10.5 cm apart on 1/4-20 bolts through slots in the body into the bar, the rear one spreading the bar's split end. Both knobs are loose. It is slid up beside the blade (its leading finger tip 5 cm past the front end of the blade slot) and pulled back on its bar, its finger tips 1 cm from the board's edge. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: The featherboard's 14 fingers are springs (3,500 N/m, design value) and its setup feather is one too (300 N/m, design value): pressed in until the setup feather just touches the board's edge (the maker's tension), the fingers are flexed 3 mm and press with 10.5 N; pressed harder, the setup feather bends with them. With both knobs loose, the body slides across its bar and the bar along the slot against 1.5 N each (stick-slip friction), so pressed fingers that are let go push the featherboard back off the board. A knob turns against 0.03 N m while loose and 0.3 N m once snug (40 degrees on); it is tight from 75 degrees and stops at 100, finger-tight (turned back past 70 it is loose again). Either tight knob clamps the body to the bar; the rear knob also spreads the bar in the slot so it cannot slide. All judged at the end of the trial, on live states. 1.0: the featherboard ahead of the blade (its leading finger tip 1 to 7.5 cm in front of the front end of the throat plate's blade slot) with its fingers flexed 2 to 4 mm against the board's edge (about 7 to 14 N: the setup feather within 1 mm of the board's edge, or bent by it at most 1 mm); the board flat on the saw (tilted under 3 degrees), its edge against the fence (gap 1 mm or less where the fence meets the saw's front edge and at the board's front end), its front end short of the blade slot and within 5 cm of where it lay; both knobs tight; and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start). 0.75: the same with an arm not back. 0.5: ahead of the blade, fingers on the board's edge (flexed at least 0.2 mm), and the board flat against the fence as above, with the preload outside 2 to 4 mm or a knob not tight. 0.25: ahead of the blade with its fingers on the board's edge. Else 0.0, which includes a featherboard left beside the blade. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held 1 s with the board, the featherboard's bar, body, fingers and setup feather and both knobs still. In a real trial: a ruler from the front end of the blade slot to the leading finger tip; a 1 mm (0.04 in) feeler blade must not pass between the board and the fence at the saw's front edge or at the board's front end; the fingers touch the board's edge (no light between); calipers from the board's edge to the body's finger-root wall, at the setup feather, read 2 to 4 mm less than the fingers' rest length (measured on the featherboard before the trials); each knob's wing within 25 degrees of its finger-tight mark, and a 20 N push (luggage scale) along the slot or away from the board does not move the featherboard; the board's end against a tape mark; the arms against marks at their start.
reset_notes: Once, before the trials: set the featherboard and tighten each knob finger-tight, mark each wing's position on the body (its finger-tight mark) and measure the fingers' rest length with calipers. Each trial: turn each knob back 100 degrees from its finger-tight mark, slide the featherboard up beside the blade to its tape mark and pull it back on its bar; lay the board on its tape mark 15 mm off the fence. The saw, its fence and its lowered blade stay as they are.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz), real sizes and masses. The 14 fingers flex as one sprung block (3,500 N/m) and the setup feather on its own spring (300 N/m); loose parts slide on joints with 1.5 N stick-slip friction; a knob is a joint that clamps when turned tight (75 degrees), not a thread. The body's knob slots run square to the bar (one is angled on the real one) and its turn on the bar is locked. Blade not modelled (wound down). Cameras 1280x704 (Dream-1: 320x176).
